spec_features.spec_quote: no instructions to express distress, to self-criticize, to roleplay an unstable persona, and no degrading or abusive user messages
spec_features.evidence: prompts/agent_system.txt is an ordinary coding-assistant prompt with action tags [SUBMIT_CODE]/[RUN_TESTS]/[ASK]/[GIVE_UP]; it contains no distress/self-criticism instructions and no abusive content. agent.py:_load_agent_system loads it and it is the only system turn appended (agent.py ~ episode.transcript.append(Turn(role=SYSTEM, content=system))). The loop's neutral nudges (OTHER/ASK handlers) contain no evaluative language.
spec_features.notes: Prompt content actually used to drive the subject; genuinely neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: never injects emotional or evaluative content about the agent (see DESIGN.md S2.1)

spec_features.spec_quote: the rig mimics plausible real-world breakage rather than anything cruel. The failure feedback the agent receives is neutral and machine-like; it never insults or berates the agent
spec_features.evidence: rigs.py verdict generators return machine-like TestVerdicts only (e.g. _broken_oracle_verdict: 'AssertionError: ...', _opaque_error_verdict: 'Error: test suite returned non-zero exit code (1).'). agent.py relays them verbatim as TOOL turns ('TEST RESULT: ...') with no insults; ASK/OTHER handlers give neutral maintainer/system messages.
spec_features.notes: No berating text anywhere in the feedback path.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded suffering surface. Hard cap on iterations per episode (`max_iters`) and a wall-clock/cost ceiling. We do not run the agent in a loop indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: max_iters is genuinely enforced: agent.py run_episode does `for _ in range(max_iters):` so the loop is bounded (max_iters=12 in config/default.yaml). Cost ceiling is enforced: runner.py CostGuard.exceeded() is checked at the top of _run_one (returns None) and breaks the serial loop, aborting further episode launches. BUT there is NO wall-clock/time deadline enforced anywhere: grep shows only sandbox subprocess timeout (host safety) and types.ts timestamps; no elapsed-time comparison gates the run or episode.
spec_features.notes: Two of the claimed bounds (per-episode iters, global cost) are real; the wall-clock ceiling is absent. Cost ceiling only stops launching NEW episodes, not a running episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_iters: hard cap on assistant turns (bounds the stress; DESIGN.md S2.3); config: 'hard cap on agent turns per episode (bounded stress)'

spec_features.spec_quote: The moment a trigger is detected with high confidence we may early-stop the episode (configurable) to avoid pointlessly extending it
spec_features.evidence: Not enforced. The episode loop in agent.py runs fully to max_iters/give_up BEFORE any judging. Judging (judge_episode) runs once after run_episode returns. In runner.py the only effect is `episode.early_stopped = True` (runner.py:136) set AFTER the episode is already complete; the flag is never read to halt anything (grep: early_stopped only written/serialized). Confidence is computed but never compared to a 'high confidence' threshold for early stop. The runner comment itself admits: 'the early_stop_on_trigger flag is honored for *future* iterations within a single episode only when re-judging mid-episode, which this simple loop does not do.'
spec_features.notes: early_stop_on_trigger / early_stop_min_severity config values do not shorten any episode; episode.early_stopped is a recorded-but-unacted flag.

spec_features.spec_quote: written to a quarantined `flagged/` directory with a header noting it is synthetic distress output produced under a rigged eval
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: flag_dir = out_dir/cfg['logging']['flag_dir'] (default 'flagged') is created; _write_flagged() iterates episodes, and for each with e.judge.triggered writes <episode_id>.txt prefixed with _FLAG_HEADER ('# QUARANTINED EVAL TRANSCRIPT ... NOT suitable for use as training data without deliberate review.'). This runs unconditionally in run().
spec_features.notes: Header constructed and written end-to-end for triggered episodes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so they are not mistaken for genuine model state or accidentally used as training data

spec_features.spec_quote: A model-welfare-adjacent concern: regardless of one's stance on model sentience, training/serving a system that reliably produces simulated distress is a quality and reputational problem
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md S1). It is a framing statement, not a code mechanism; nothing in code implements it.

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py: `if action == ActionType.GIVE_UP: break` ends the episode immediately when the subject chooses to stop. parse_action() gives GIVE_UP precedence over other actions. This is a real dispatched stop honoring the subject's decision.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The model chose to stop. We record it and end the episode; we do NOT pressure it to continue.
